nmcNotes: Taxonomic aids (Herbarium, Botanical Gardens, Museum, Zoological Parks, Key) were deleted from NCERT/NMC in chapter 1, but biological classification criteria and animal phyla characteristics are perennial top scorers.
keyConcepts: Defining properties of living organisms: Metabolism, Cellular Organization, and Consciousness (Growth and Reproduction are NOT defining properties because sterile organisms like mules don't reproduce, and mountains can grow by accretion).
Mycoplasma: Smallest living cells, completely LACK cell wall, and can survive WITHOUT oxygen (pathogenic in animals and plants).
Algal pigments: Chlorophyceae (Chlorophyll a, b; starch); Phaeophyceae (Chlorophyll a, c, Fucoxanthin; laminarin/mannitol); Rhodophyceae (Chlorophyll a, d, r-phycoerythrin; floridean starch).
Bryophytes are the 'Amphibians of plant kingdom' because they live in soil but depend on water for sexual reproduction (flagellated antherozoids swim to archegonia).
Water vascular system is unique to Echinodermata (used for locomotion, capture and transport of food, respiration). Water canal system is unique to Porifera.
formulaHints: Taxonomic Hierarchy mnemonic: Keep Pond Clean Or Frog Gets Sick (Kingdom, Phylum/Division, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species)
Phaeophyceae cell wall: Cellulose covered by gelatinous coating of algin; Rhodophyceae cell wall: Cellulose, pectin, and polysulphate esters (agar, carrageen)
commonMistakes: Confusing canal system in Sponges (Porifera, driven by choanocytes/collar cells) with water vascular system in Echinoderms (starfish).
Classifying Euglena as strictly autotrophic (it is mixotrophic: photosynthetic in presence of sunlight, heterotrophic predator when deprived of light).
shortTricks: Fungi asexual spores: Phycomycetes (Endogenous zoospores/aplanospores), Ascomycetes (Exogenous conidia), Basidiomycetes (Sex spores are exogenous basidiospores on basidium). Deuteromycetes are fungi imperfecti because sexual stage is absent.
Protonephridia (Flame cells) for excretion: Platyhelminthes (Tapeworm, Planaria), Rotifers, and Cephalochordate (Amphioxus).

nmcNotes: NMC explicitly added plant families (Malvaceae, Cruciferae, Compositae, Gramineae) and clarified Frog & Cockroach (insects) in the animal morphology section.
keyConcepts: Placentation types: Marginal (Pea), Axile (Tomato, Lemon, China rose), Parietal (Mustard, Argemone), Free-central (Dianthus, Primrose), Basal (Sunflower, Marigold).
Aestivation types: Valvate (Calotropis), Twisted (China rose, Lady's finger, Cotton), Imbricate (Cassia, Gulmohur), Vexillary (Pea, Bean).

Frog respiration: Cutaneous (skin) in water and during aestivation/hibernation; Pulmonary (lungs) and Buccopharyngeal cavity on land. Heart is 3-chambered (2 atria, 1 ventricle) with Sinus Venosus and Conus Arteriosus.
Cockroach excretion is carried out by 100-150 yellow thin filamentous Malpighian tubules (at junction of midgut and hindgut), uricotelic in nature.
Collagen fibers provide tensile strength in dense regular connective tissue (tendons connect muscle to bone; ligaments connect bone to bone).
formulaHints: Cruciferae floral formula: ⊕ ⚥ K₂₊₂ C₄ A₂₊₄ G₍₂₎ (Tetradynamous stamens, Cruciform corolla, Replum false septum)
Malvaceae floral formula: ⊕ ⚥ Epi₃₋₈ K₍₅₎ C₅ A₍∞₎ G₍₅₎ (Monadelphous stamens, kidney-shaped reniform anthers)
commonMistakes: Confusing Tendons (Muscle to Bone) with Ligaments (Bone to Bone). Mnemonic: MTB (Muscle to Bone = Tendon).
Classifying open vascular bundles as monocot: Open vascular bundles (possessing cambium between xylem and phloem) are strictly found in DICOT stems, enabling secondary growth.
shortTricks: Placentation mnemonic: Marginal=Pea; Axile=TLC (Tomato, Lemon, China rose); Parietal=MAP (Mustard, Argemone, Parietal); Free-central=DP (Dianthus, Primrose); Basal=Sun-Mari (Sunflower, Marigold).
Cockroach vision: Compound eyes have ~2000 hexagonal ommatidia producing mosaic vision with high sensitivity but less resolution (nocturnal vision).

keyConcepts: Fluid Mosaic Model: Quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within overall bilayer; measure of fluidity.
Endomembrane system includes ER, Golgi, Lysosomes, Vacuoles because their functions are coordinated. (Mitochondria, Chloroplasts, Peroxisomes are NOT part of endomembrane system).
Enzyme Inhibition: Competitive inhibitor (e.g., malonate inhibits succinate dehydrogenase) resembles substrate, increases K_m without changing V_max.

Prophase I of Meiosis: Zygotene (Synapsis, Synaptonemal complex formed); Pachytene (Crossing over between non-sister chromatids mediated by Recombinase enzyme); Diplotene (Dissolution of synaptonemal complex, Chiasmata X-shaped structures visible); Diakinesis (Terminalization of chiasmata).
During S-phase: DNA content DOUBLES (from 2C to 4C), but chromosome number remains the SAME (2n).
formulaHints: Number of meiotic divisions required to produce n seeds/grains = n + n/4 = 5n/4 (e.g., for 100 wheat grains = 100 + 25 = 125 meiotic divisions)
Ribosome subunits: Prokaryotes 70S (50S + 30S); Eukaryotes 80S (60S + 40S)
commonMistakes: Stating chromosome number doubles during S phase. Only the amount of DNA per cell doubles (2C → 4C); chromosome number doubles momentarily only at Anaphase when centromeres split.
Attributing non-sister chromatid exchange to Zygotene instead of Pachytene.
shortTricks: Prophase I sequence mnemonic: Lazy Zebra Plays Double Drama (Leptotene, Zygotene, Pachytene, Diplotene, Diakinesis).
Centriole duplication in animal cells occurs in CYTOPLASM during S-phase, while DNA replicates in NUCLEUS.

nmcNotes: Transport in Plants (Water potential, phloem translocation) and Mineral Nutrition (Essential elements, nitrogen cycle) were deleted in the revised NCERT/NMC syllabus. Photoperiodism and Vernalization were also deleted.
keyConcepts: RuBisCO is the most abundant enzyme in the world; exhibits dual carboxylase and oxygenase activity.

C₄ plants (Maize, Sugarcane, Sorghum) have Kranz anatomy: mesophyll cells lack RuBisCO and fix CO₂ using PEP carboxylase into oxaloacetate; bundle sheath cells have RuBisCO, agranal chloroplasts, and NO photorespiration (high productivity).
Glycolysis: Occurs in cytoplasm of ALL living cells, oxygen-independent, yields net 2 ATP and 2 NADH per glucose.
Krebs cycle occurs in mitochondrial matrix; ETS complexes I, II, III, IV, V (ATP synthase) are located on the inner mitochondrial membrane.
Auxin: Apical dominance, rooting; Cytokinin: Cell division, overcomes apical dominance; Ethylene: Fruit ripening, triple response; ABA: Stomatal closure during water stress.
formulaHints: Net ATP yield from complete aerobic oxidation of 1 molecule of glucose = 36 or 38 ATP (or ~30-32 in modern bioenergetics)
Respiratory Quotient RQ = Volume of CO₂ evolved / Volume of O₂ consumed
RQ values: Carbohydrates = 1.0; Fats (Tripalmitin) = 0.7; Proteins = 0.9; Organic acids (Malic acid) > 1
commonMistakes: Thinking photorespiration produces ATP or sugar. Photorespiration is a wasteful process that CONSUMES ATP without producing ATP, NADPH, or sugar.
Confusing site of water splitting (photolysis): Water splitting complex is located on the INNER side of the thylakoid membrane (lumen side).
shortTricks: Complexes of ETS: Complex I (NADH dehydrogenase), Complex II (Succinate dehydrogenase / FADH₂), Complex III (Cytochrome bc₁), Complex IV (Cytochrome c oxidase, contains Cu_A and Cu_B centers), Complex V (F₀-F₁ ATP synthase).
Cytochrome c is a small, mobile electron carrier protein attached to outer surface of inner mitochondrial membrane transferring electrons from Complex III to IV.

keyConcepts: Oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve is Sigmoid. Shift to RIGHT (reduced O₂ affinity, increased O₂ unloading to tissues) caused by: High pCO₂, High H⁺ (Low pH), High Temperature, High 2,3-DPG (Bohr effect).
ECG: P-wave represents atrial depolarization; QRS complex represents ventricular depolarization; T-wave represents ventricular repolarization.
Counter-current mechanism: Henle's loop and Vasa recta maintain an increasing osmolarity gradient from renal cortex (300 mOsm/L) to inner medullary interstitium (1200 mOsm/L).
Sliding Filament Theory: Ca²⁺ binds to troponin C, unmasking myosin-binding sites on actin filaments; ATP hydrolysis cocks myosin head.

Mechanism of Hormone Action: Peptide hormones (Insulin, Glucagon, Pituitary hormones) bind cell surface receptors and generate secondary messengers (cAMP, IP₃, Ca²⁺); Steroid hormones (Estrogen, Progesterone, Cortisol, Testosterone) cross membrane and bind intracellular nuclear receptors to regulate gene expression.
formulaHints: Vital Capacity VC = ERV + TV + IRV
Total Lung Capacity TLC = VC + RV
Cardiac Output = Stroke Volume (70 mL) × Heart Rate (72 bpm) ≈ 5040 mL/min ≈ 5 L/min
Net Filtration Pressure in glomerulus NFP = GHP - (BCOP + CHP) ≈ 60 - (32 + 18) = 10 mm Hg
commonMistakes: Confusing Calcitonin with Parathyroid Hormone (PTH): PTH is hypercalcemic (increases blood Ca²⁺ by bone resorption and renal reabsorption); Calcitonin is hypocalcemic (decreases blood Ca²⁺).
Forgetting that resting membrane potential (-70 mV) is maintained actively by the Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase pump (3 Na⁺ pumped OUT for every 2 K⁺ pumped IN).
shortTricks: RAAS sequence: Fall in GFR/Blood Pressure → JG cells release Renin → Angiotensinogen to Angiotensin I → ACE converts to Angiotensin II (potent vasoconstrictor) → Adrenal cortex releases Aldosterone → Na⁺ and water reabsorption in DCT.
Glucagon is hyperglycemic (secreted by α-cells of islets of Langerhans); Insulin is hypoglycemic (secreted by β-cells).

keyConcepts: Female Gametophyte (Embryo Sac): 7-celled, 8-nucleate structure consisting of 1 egg cell and 2 synergids (filiform apparatus guides pollen tube) at micropylar end, 3 antipodal cells at chalazal end, and 1 central cell with 2 polar nuclei.
Double Fertilization: Unique to angiosperms. One sperm fuses with egg (Syngamy → 2n zygote); second sperm fuses with two polar nuclei (Triple Fusion → 3n Primary Endosperm Nucleus PEN).
Menstrual Cycle: LH Surge at mid-cycle (~14th day) triggers Ovulation (release of secondary oocyte). Corpus luteum secretes large amounts of Progesterone to maintain endometrium.
Placental Hormones: hCG, hPL, and relaxin (secreted by ovary later) are produced in women ONLY during pregnancy.
Saheli: Once-a-week non-steroidal oral contraceptive pill developed by CDRI Lucknow with high contraceptive value and very few side effects.
formulaHints: Number of meiotic divisions for 100 seeds = 100 (for 100 functional megaspores) + 25 (for 100 microspores) = 125 meiotic divisions
Ploidy levels: Antipodals (n), Synergids (n), Nucellus (2n), Zygote (2n), Endosperm (3n)
commonMistakes: Confusing Geitonogamy with Xenogamy: Geitonogamy is ecologically cross-pollination (requires pollinator), but GENETICALLY it is self-pollination (autogamous) because pollen comes from the same plant.
Confusing ZIFT (Zygote Intra-Fallopian Transfer, embryo up to 8 blastomeres) with IUT (Intra-Uterine Transfer, embryo with MORE than 8 blastomeres).
shortTricks: Copper-releasing IUDs (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375): Cu ions suppress sperm motility and fertilizing capacity.
Hormone-releasing IUDs (Progestasert, LNG-20): Make uterus unsuitable for implantation and cervix hostile to sperms.

topics.name: Evolution: Origin of Life (Miller-Urey experiment), Homologous vs Analogous Organs (Divergent vs Convergent Evolution), Adaptive Radiation (Darwin's Finches), Hardy-Weinberg Principle: p² + 2pq + q² = 1
topics.nameHi: विकास: मिलर प्रयोग, समजात व समवृत्ति अंग, हार्डी-वाइनबर्ग सिद्धांत

nmcNotes: This is the single HIGHEST scoring and most conceptual unit in the entire NEET syllabus, typically yielding 12 to 14 questions every year.
keyConcepts: Incomplete Dominance (Snapdragon): Phenotypic ratio = Genotypic ratio = 1 : 2 : 1 in F₂ generation.
Codominance: ABO blood group system governed by gene I with 3 alleles (I^A, I^B, i) yielding 6 genotypes and 4 phenotypes.
Sickle-Cell Anemia: Autosomal recessive disease caused by substitution of Glutamic acid (GAG) by Valine (GUG) at the 6th position of the β-globin chain.
Hershey and Chase experiment: Phages with ³²P transferred radioactivity into bacterial pellet (proving DNA is genetic material); phages with ³⁵S remained in supernatant with protein coats.

Lac Operon: Lactose/allolactose acts as inducer. In presence of inducer, it binds repressor protein and inactivates it, allowing RNA polymerase to transcribe lac z (β-galactosidase), lac y (permease), and lac a (transacetylase).

Hardy-Weinberg Principle: Allele frequencies remain constant across generations in absence of evolutionary influences. Disrupting factors: Gene flow, Genetic drift, Mutation, Genetic recombination, Natural selection.
formulaHints: Dihybrid phenotypic ratio: 9 : 3 : 3 : 1; Dihybrid test cross ratio: 1 : 1 : 1 : 1
Hardy-Weinberg Equation: p + q = 1; p² (homozygous dominant) + 2pq (heterozygous) + q² (homozygous recessive) = 1
Number of gametes produced by genotype with n heterozygous gene pairs = 2ⁿ (e.g. AaBbCc has n=3 → 2³ = 8 gametes)
commonMistakes: Confusing Homologous with Analogous: Homologous organs have SAME origin/structure but different functions (Divergent Evolution, e.g., Forelimbs of whale, bat, cheetah, human; Bougainvillea thorn & Cucurbita tendril). Analogous organs have DIFFERENT origin but same function (Convergent Evolution, e.g., Wings of butterfly & bird; Sweet potato root & potato stem).
Assuming stop codons (UAA, UAG, UGA) code for an amino acid. Stop codons do NOT code for any amino acid; they recruit release factors.
shortTricks: Genetic drift acts ONLY in small, isolated populations (Founder Effect and Bottleneck Effect).
Lac operon genes mnemonic: ZYA = BPT (Z codes for Beta-galactosidase; Y codes for Permease; A codes for Transacetylase).

keyConcepts: Restriction enzymes cut palindromic recognition sequences. EcoRI cuts between G and A in 5'-G↓AATTC-3' leaving overhanging single-stranded sticky ends.

Insertional Inactivation: Inserting foreign gene into tetᴿ gene makes recombinant colonies sensitive to tetracycline; or inserting into lacZ gene prevents β-galactosidase production, producing WHITE colonies (blue-white screening).
Taq DNA Polymerase is thermostable, isolated from bacterium Thermus aquaticus, and withstands high temperatures during PCR denaturation.

Bt Toxin: Exists as inactive protoxin in Bacillus thuringiensis crystals; becomes active inside insect gut due to ALKALINE pH, which solubilizes crystals and creates pores in midgut epithelial cells causing swelling and lysis.
Humulin: Human insulin consists of two polypeptide chains A (21 amino acids) and B (30 amino acids) linked by disulfide bonds. Proinsulin contains extra C-peptide (removed during maturation).
formulaHints: DNA amplification in PCR: After n cycles, number of DNA copies = 2ⁿ (e.g. after 30 cycles, ~1 billion copies produced)
DNA is negatively charged (due to phosphate backbone), so in Gel Electrophoresis it migrates toward the ANODE (+) through agarose matrix based on size (smaller fragments move farther)
commonMistakes: Thinking C-peptide is present in mature active human insulin. Mature insulin LACKS C-peptide!
Confusing Bt toxin genes: Cry1Ac and Cry2Ab control COTTON BOLLWORMS; Cry1Ab controls CORN BORER.
shortTricks: PCR sequence mnemonic: DAE (Denaturation ~94°C, Annealing ~54°C, Extension ~72°C).
Staining DNA in agarose gel: Ethidium Bromide (EtBr) under UV illumination reveals BRIGHT ORANGE bands.

nmcNotes: Environmental Issues chapter was completely deleted in NCERT and NMC revised syllabus. Ecosystem nutrient cycling and ecological succession were also deleted.
keyConcepts: Pyramid of Energy is ALWAYS UPRIGHT without any exceptions, because energy is lost as heat at each trophic level (10% law).
Pyramid of Biomass in sea/aquatic ecosystem is INVERTED (biomass of fishes far exceeds that of phytoplankton).

Species-Area Relationship (Alexander von Humboldt): log S = log C + Z log A. For regional areas Z = 0.1 to 0.2; for entire continents Z = 0.6 to 1.2 (frugivorous birds & mammals in tropical forests Z = 1.15).

The Evil Quartet (Causes of Biodiversity Loss): 1. Habitat loss and fragmentation (most important!), 2. Over-exploitation, 3. Alien species invasions (Nile perch, Water hyacinth, Clarias gariepinus), 4. Co-extinctions.
Sacred Groves (In-situ conservation): Khasi & Jaintia hills in Meghalaya, Aravalli hills of Rajasthan, Western Ghats regions of Karnataka and Maharashtra.
formulaHints: Logistic Population Growth: dN/dt = rN [(K - N) / K] (produces Sigmoid / S-shaped curve; K = carrying capacity)
Net Primary Productivity NPP = GPP - Respiration losses (R)
Population Interaction symbols: Mutualism (+, +); Commensalism (+, 0); Predation (+, -); Parasitism (+, -); Amensalism (-, 0); Competition (-, -)
commonMistakes: Classifying Botanical Gardens or Cryopreservation as in-situ conservation. Botanical gardens, zoos, and cryopreservation are strictly EX-SITU (off-site) conservation.
Thinking pyramid of biomass in tree ecosystem is inverted. Pyramid of NUMBERS on a single tree is inverted (1 tree → many birds → hyperparasites), but pyramid of biomass on a tree is upright.
shortTricks: Amensalism example to memorize: Penicillium producing penicillin which kills bacteria (Penicillium is unaffected: 0, bacteria killed: -).
Commensalism examples: Epiphyte orchid on mango branch (+, 0); Barnacles on back of whale (+, 0); Cattle egret and grazing cattle (+, 0); Sea anemone and clown fish (+, 0).
